title: Man. Post. Cap. II duplex: Est igitur quaestio — Immediata defined; Placeus denies
pass_a_gloss: Est igitur: There is therefore a question instituted among us only concerning the first sin of Adam taken in the first mode, that is, concerning his actual disobedience, concerning that internal and external action by which he transgressed God's law by act, cut off from the habitual corruption which followed that action: whether it is imputed to us being born? To which question it seems satisfaction must be given not yet by a simple negation, but again by a distinction. For its attribute must be distinguished. For a twofold imputation can be conceived in the mind. Immediate and Mediate, or (as I may say the same in other words) Antecedent and Consequent. I call Immediate that which alone I wished to deny by the theses which you took upon yourself to refute; by which that action of Adam, that is, his Eating of the forbidden fruit, is thought to be imputed to all his posterity (Christ excepted) proximately, immediately, by this itself that they are sons of Adam, unto those two punishments properly so called, the privation of original righteousness which you call spiritual death, and eternal death. This alone imputation of that action I have denied, because it is not taught in the sacred letters by the adequate norm of our faith, because it fights with the sacred letters, because it makes God author of sin, because it dishonors God's justice, because from it it follows that Christ is a sinner by his nature, because it draws with itself some other absurdities obscuring the wonderful purity and splendor of the Christian religion, which would that our brothers and fellow-servants, warned by me through the theses, had either not wholly despised, or not contemptuously weighed!
pass_b_english: So the question between us concerns only Adam's first sin in the first sense—his actual disobedience, that inward and outward act by which he broke God's law, cut off from the habitual corruption that followed it: is that act imputed to us at birth? A bare no will not settle it; the attribute of the question must again be distinguished. One may conceive a twofold imputation: Immediate and Mediate, or—same point in other words—Antecedent and Consequent. By Immediate I mean the only imputation I meant to deny in the theses you undertook to refute: the view that Adam's act itself—his eating the forbidden fruit—is charged to all his posterity (Christ excepted) immediately, simply because they are Adam's children, unto the two punishments properly so called: loss of original righteousness (which you call spiritual death) and eternal death. That alone I have denied—because Scripture, the adequate rule of our faith, does not teach it; because it clashes with Scripture; because it makes God the author of sin; because it dishonors God's justice; because it would make Christ a sinner by nature; and because it drags other absurdities that cloud the purity and glory of the Christian religion. Would that our brothers and fellow servants, warned by those theses, had neither wholly scorned them nor weighed them with contempt!
source_text: Est igitur quaestio inter nos instituta duntaxat de primo peccato Adami sumpto primo modo, hoc est, de actuali ejus inobedientia, de actione illa interna & externa, qua Dei legem transgressus est actu, praecisa ab habituali corruptione, qua actionem illam secuta est: num ea nobis nascentibus imputetur? Cui quaestioni nondum negatione simplici, sed distinctione rursus satisfaciendum videtur. Est enim ejus distinguendum attributum. Potest enim animo concipi duplex imputatio. Immediata & Mediata, vel (ut idem aliis verbis dicam) Antecedens & Consequens. Immediatam voco eam, quam solam thesibus, quas tu refutandas tibi sumpsisti, negare volui; qua putatur actio illa Adami, hoc est, vetiti fructus Manducatio ejus posteris omnibus (Christo excepto) proxime, immediate, hoc ipso quod filii sunt Adami, imputari ad duas istas poenas proprie dictas, privationem justitiae originalis quam mortem spiritualem appellas, & mortem aeternam. Hanc solam imputationem actionis illius ego negavi, quia non docetur in sacris literis adaequata fidei nostrae norma, quia pugnat cum sacris literis, quia Deum facit authorem peccati, quia Dei justitiam dehonestat, quia sequitur ex ea Christum esse natura sua peccatorem, quia alia nonnulla trahit secum absurda, mirabilem religionis Christianae puritatem & splendorem obscurantia, quae utinam fratres & conservi nostri a me per theses moniti, aut non prorsus contempsissent, aut non contemptim expendissent!
